correctness.rationale: An active root edge survives precisely when isolated as a component, while an inactive edge becomes active precisely when both endpoints are isolated vertices. Thus F(S)=I(S)⊔E(U(S)). Independently, undirected open NOR is antitone with S⊆F²(S); applying this twice in the two directions gives F³=F. The complement W of the isolated vertices and isolated-edge matching supports components of order at least three, so |W| is zero or at least three. Substituting |U|≤1, |U|=2, and |U|≥3 in the image formula gives exactly the fixed matchings and the two disjoint classes of cycles; when |U|=2 its edge joins the matching, rather than forming a separate clique case. A two-edge path is not an image and realizes one-step entry. Fibres of a clique phase of order at least three uniquely specify the isolated vertices and matching. For a matching phase its fibre additionally allows replacing at most one matching edge by two isolated vertices, which gives the extra m·a_r term and the perfect/near-perfect distinction. Removing labelled components of orders one and two gives the EGF; counting unordered complementary parts gives the orbit census. For the dominant basin the complement is the union of pair-isolation and isolated-edge events with the empty graph removed. Each event prescribes 2n−3 bits; compatible shared-endpoint pairs prescribe at least 3n−6 and disjoint pairs 4n−10. Bonferroni yields the displayed relative O(n·2^(−n)) error; the empty graph correction is smaller. The union bound gives strict majority for n≥4, and n=3 gives 5/8. An independent truth-table enumeration checked F³=F and every individual basin through n=7, including 2,097,152 inputs there and distinguished basin 2,059,625.
residual_risks: The finite replay supplements the all-n proof rather than proving it. The asymptotic uses independent fair bits; the deterministic basin statements do not. The symbol E_n is overloaded in the record for the edge set and fixed-state count, with the intended meaning clear from context.

evidence: Aledo et al. give periods at most two and periodic/fixed-point enumeration methods or bounds. Aracena et al. give fix(G⁻)=mis(G). Gadouleau–Kutner study the same MIS operation under sequential updating. The same-day coning theorem describes a basin lift on H∨K_r.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These establish generic periodicity, fixed points or a transformation for coned graphs, not the component constraints and exact fibres here. For n≥4 each root edge has a disjoint root edge, so the triangular network has no universal vertex and is not a nontrivial clique cone.

value.rationale: This is a natural synchronous rule on a canonical line-graph family, and generic two-periodicity leaves the distribution of initial states among orbits unresolved. Exact sizes of every individual basin expose both the matching skeleton and an explicit effect of excluding self-neighbors, including the change in the sharp leading rare-event coefficient. The classification and phase-resolved counts are materially more informative than an orbit census or a mere concentration bound.
residual_risks: No general result for arbitrary line graphs or other update schedules is established.
